The prototype is easy to navigate from my assigned perspective/role as a faculty adviser. The content is also simple and easy to understand. Based on my experience, the only area I would suggest improving is the Tasks (instructions).
The system was so easy to navigate and use

Overall Impression

The task flow was clear and easy to complete. The navigation is simple, the layout is consistent across pages, and the create → save draft → reopen → edit → save steps followed a logical order. The one real friction point was working out how to select the student to evaluate. Fixing that would remove the main barrier to an otherwise smooth experience.

What Works Well

A. Simple, consistent navigation. The four-item sidebar (Dashboard, Students, Evaluations, Documents) uses clear labels and icons, and the active page is highlighted.

B. Clear page headers. Each page has a title and a one-line description of its purpose, such as “Manage your assigned internship evaluations.”

C. Useful status summary on Evaluations. The Total, Draft, and Submitted cards let an adviser see their workload at a glance.

D. Prominent primary action. The dark “New Evaluation” button is easy to find and stands out from the rest of the page.

E. Familiar data table. Search, filter, column, density, and full-screen controls plus pagination work as users expect.

F. Draft workflow. Letting advisers save and revise before submitting suits how evaluations are actually done.

Areas for Improvement

A. Student selection in New Evaluation (High priority)

This was the main difficulty you reported. Likely causes, based on what the pages show:

1. The Evaluations list only shows students who already have an evaluation. The Students page lists the advisee pool, but the Evaluations page lists a different set of people (at least in the visible rows). An adviser may not realize that the New Evaluation form is where new interns are chosen.

2. No visible cue about eligibility. The task notes that each intern can have only one Faculty Adviser evaluation, but the interface doesn’t appear to show which interns are eligible, already evaluated, or have a pending internship status.

3. The Students page doesn’t connect to evaluating. The row’s only action is a “view” (eye) icon.

Recommendations:

- Make the student field a searchable dropdown or autocomplete showing name, student number, and program.

- Show each intern’s evaluation state in the picker (“No evaluation yet”, “Draft”, “Submitted”), and disable or flag interns who already have one with a short explanation.

- Add a label or helper text such as “Select the student intern you want to evaluate.”

- Add an “Evaluate” action on the Students page that opens the form with that student pre-selected.

- If interns with a “Pending” internship status can’t be evaluated, say so in the picker rather than leaving users to guess.

B. Evaluations table readability (Medium)

1. Columns are cut off, so “Evaluation Type” and its values appear as “Evalua…” and “Facult…”. Users must scroll or guess to read them.

2. There is no Status column, such as Draft or Submitted, even though the summary cards track it. Advisers can’t tell which row is a draft without opening it.

3. The pencil (edit) icon has no tooltip or text label, so its function isn’t obvious.

Recommendations: Set sensible column widths or allow wrapping, put Status in the first few columns with a color-coded chip, and add tooltips such as “Edit evaluation” to icon-only actions.

C. Feedback and confirmation after saving (Medium)

1. Tasks 6 and 10 ask evaluators to verify saves, which suggests the confirmation needs to be unmistakable. If it isn’t already:

- Show a clear success message (“Draft saved”) and update the Draft counter and table row immediately.
- Show a “last saved” timestamp inside the draft.
- Warn users about unsaved changes if they navigate away.


D. Form clarity (Medium)

- Define each rating scale (what a 1 or a 5 means) near the input.
- Show a live summary or computed total so changes to ratings are visible.
- Make “Save as Draft” and “Submit” visually distinct, so users don’t submit accidentally. The black background does a little bit of it but not much

E. Dashboard value (Low to Medium)

The dashboard states “Monitor assigned students and internship progress,” but it only shows a welcome message and role. Useful additions would be counts of assigned interns, evaluations pending or in draft, and shortcuts such as “Create evaluation.” The greeting also shows a shortened name, while the header shows the full name with suffix (Jr. vs No Jr.). Pick one convention.

F. Smaller observations (Low)

A. Documents page: “Approved” and “Pending” are pale gray text with weak contrast, and the download icon has no label. Color-coded status chips would read better.

B. Disabled Upload button: It’s gray with no hint why. A note like “Select a document type and file to enable upload” would help.

C. Mixed terminology: Pages use “Student Intern,” “Student,” and “Intern / Internship.” One consistent term would reduce confusion.

D. Accessibility: Check color contrast on secondary text, keyboard access to icon buttons, and ARIA labels for the table action icons.

Closing Remarks

The system does what it sets out to do, and the drafting workflow is easy to follow once the right student is selected. The suggestions above mostly concern discoverability and feedback, such as helping users find where to start and confirming what they did, rather than structural problems. With a better student selection experience and clearer status indicators, I expect the task to be completed without hesitation even by first-time users. Well done to the team, and I hope this helps in refining the system.
